No lens failed; verification-gap lens ran clean (no findings).

findings.title: Commit subjects violate documented format
findings.problem: All 9 commits in range use 'EPMCDME-14574 : <Capitalized description>' instead of the documented '<type>: <short description>' form (type in feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor, no ticket prefix).
findings.impact: Breaks the documented squash-merge workflow where the MR description (not per-commit subjects) becomes the final commit body, and diverges from the repo's stated commit-format standard.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite subjects to the documented form, e.g. 'fix: match Connections screen to parent-story design and spec'.

findings.title: VS Code checks parse content, spec says existence-only
findings.problem: spec.md's Non-goal states config-file checks are file-existence only, never reading/interpreting contents. vscode_copilot_connected (line 43) parses chatLanguageModels.json and matches vendor/name fields; vscode_claude_code_connected (line 55) parses settings.json and checks specific env-var names.
findings.impact: plan.md documents a deliberate, researched override (the spec's named path getters live only in an unreachable external CLI package), but spec.md itself was never updated, so the frozen acceptance criterion still reads as violated -- a human call is needed on whether to update spec.md to record the correction or revert to pure existence checks (which would likely make VS Code detection unusably coarse).
findings.recommendation: Update spec.md to record the researched exception (preferred, since a pure existence check can't distinguish a CodeMie entry from any other JSON content), or get explicit sign-off to keep the deviation undocumented.

findings.title: home_dir() silently defaults when HOME/USERPROFILE unset
findings.problem: home_dir() falls back to an empty string via unwrap_or_default() when neither HOME nor USERPROFILE is set in the process env.
findings.impact: Every downstream path (e.g. '/Library/Application Support/...') resolves relative to '/' instead, and check_connector_status silently reports every row as not-connected with no error surfaced, instead of signalling a broken environment.
findings.recommendation: Return an Option/Result from home_dir() and have check_connector_status surface a distinct error/unknown state when HOME cannot be resolved, instead of defaulting to an empty string.

findings.title: Hardcoded macOS paths under an active Windows build target
findings.problem: home_dir()'s USERPROFILE fallback implies Windows support, but check_connector_status only ever builds macOS-only paths ('Library/Application Support/...'). tauri.conf.json's bundle.targets includes 'nsis' (a real Windows installer target), and the rest of this codebase gates platform-specific paths behind #[cfg(target_os = ...)] (see app_updater.rs, pathman.rs, steps.rs) -- this file doesn't follow that convention.
findings.impact: On a Windows build, check_connector_status silently reports every connector as disconnected with no error, rather than erroring or using Windows-appropriate paths -- the entire Connections feature is non-functional there with no indication anything is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Gate connectors.rs's path construction behind #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] / add a Windows-appropriate branch, matching the convention already used in app_updater.rs and pathman.rs.

findings.title: VS Code Insiders fallback skipped on malformed/non-matching stable file
findings.problem: vscode_chat_models_path/vscode_settings_path fall back from stable 'Code' to 'Code - Insiders' only when the stable file is missing or empty (.filter(|s| !s.is_empty())) -- not when it exists but is malformed or simply doesn't contain a CodeMie entry.
findings.impact: A user with CodeMie wired up only in VS Code Insiders, while a non-matching (but non-empty/valid-JSON) chatLanguageModels.json or settings.json exists for stable Code, never has the Insiders file consulted -- the row incorrectly reports not-connected.
findings.recommendation: Read both stable and Insiders files and OR the parsed results, rather than gating the Insiders read on the stable file being empty/missing.

findings.title: app_bundle_exists ignores ~/Applications
findings.impact: Apps installed via Homebrew cask or any non-admin install into the user's own ~/Applications are reported not-installed, permanently blocking the connect/disconnect UI for that row even though the app is present.

findings.title: findProxyConnectError regex misses mixed-case 'Failed:' prefix
findings.problem: The regex /^\s*(✗|[Ee]rror:|FAILED:|failed:)/ only matches all-caps 'FAILED:' or all-lowercase 'failed:', not a mixed-case prefix like 'Failed:'.
findings.impact: If the CLI ever emits a mixed-case failure prefix, a genuine failure line is not recognized and the user sees the generic exit-code message instead of the real CLI error text.
findings.recommendation: Broaden the alternation to a case-insensitive match, e.g. /^\s*(✗|[Ee]rror:|[Ff][Aa][Ii][Ll][Ee][Dd]:)/.

findings.title: Auth-gate notice hardcodes 'Claude Desktop' for all apps
findings.problem: ensureAuthenticated()'s blocked-state message still reads "Connecting Claude Desktop needs a signed-in CodeMie profile…" even though the gate now fires for VS Code Copilot, VS Code Claude Code, and Codex desktop row actions too.
findings.impact: A user trying to connect VS Code or Codex desktop while signed out sees a notice that names the wrong app, which is confusing and looks like a bug in the wizard routing.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize the notice text with the action/app name, or use app-agnostic wording.

findings.title: IPC failures rendered identical to 'not configured'
findings.problem: refreshConnectionsView swallows bridge.connectors.checkStatus() failure into {} and bridge.runner.runCapture() failure into { stdout: '' }, both of which then compute as 'nothing configured / daemon down'.
findings.impact: A backend or IPC outage is indistinguishable from a genuinely not-connected state; the user sees misleading 'Not set'/'Disconnected' rows with no indication anything failed.
findings.recommendation: On catch, mark the view with a distinct error/loading state (e.g. a banner or per-row 'status unavailable') instead of defaulting to empty/falsy values that feed the normal status computation.

findings.title: runConnectionRowAction duplicates runAction instead of reusing it
findings.problem: runConnectionRowAction reimplements openTerminal/spawnPty/writeLine handling rather than calling the existing runAction() helper (renderer.js:354), because runAction's fixed onClose: () => showView(returnView) would navigate away from the Connections screen instead of refreshing it.
findings.impact: Two near-identical PTY-action code paths now need to be kept in sync; a future fix (e.g. CR-007's parser hookup) applied to one is easy to miss in the other.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional onClose override parameter to runAction() and have runConnectionRowAction call it with onClose: () => refreshConnectionsView(), removing the duplicated logic.

findings.title: Disconnect stdout is never scanned for errors
findings.problem: The engine:pty-data listener and findProxyConnectError call are gated on isConnect (action.kind === 'connect'/'reconnect'); disconnect actions never have their PTY output buffered or parsed.
findings.impact: A 'codemie proxy disconnect' failure reported via stdout (rather than a non-zero exit code) is never surfaced to the user -- they only ever see the generic exit-code message, contradicting the task's 'reflect result' requirement for disconnect.
findings.recommendation: Drop the isConnect gate on the buffer/listener and findProxyConnectError call so disconnect output is scanned the same way as connect output.

findings.title: Malformed PTY data chunk silently dropped
findings.problem: The engine:pty-data handler's try { buf += atob(e.payload.data); } catch { /* ignore */ } silently drops a chunk if atob() throws on malformed/partial base64.
findings.impact: Part of a genuine error line can be silently lost from buf, causing findProxyConnectError to miss a real CLI failure and fall back to the generic exit-code message.
findings.recommendation: On catch, log the decode failure or mark the buffer as possibly-truncated so a lost chunk isn't silently treated as clean output.
